attributes.residual: TWO named mechanisms, both read three times with byte-identical output. (a) CTR LOOP, 4 of the remaining rows: target emits a plain top-tested counter loop (cmpw r29,r7 / bge -> epilogue ... addi r29,r29,1 / b back to the test) while we emit MWCC's strength-reduced counted loop (cmpwi/mtctr/ble ... bdnz). Both sides hoist e->count once before the loop and neither loop body contains a call, so the CTR transform is legal for both - this is MWCC's loop optimiser declining the reduction in the target, not a source-visible difference. Three distinct axes all produced BYTE-IDENTICAL output: for-form vs while-form; caching the bound in a named local (nlines = e->count) via a conserving pad split; and an inner-block accumulator temp (s32 h = ...; total += h). AXIS CLOSED at 3. (b) ONE target-only `mr r3,r0` in the idx>=0 return path, where we compute directly into r3 - the TARGET-only home-copy direction that claim.law.callee-saved-home-copy-coalescing-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v1 documents as source-unreachable. MEASUREMENT RESOLUTION: frame read off the stwu constant and cross-checked with an alias-aware dump of every N(r1) displacement on both sides; all seven slot displacements are identical (64/68/72/76/80/96/108) and low_gap is 56 on both sides. CALIBRATION MISFIRE WORTH REUSING: the inlined-callee-frames law predicts an expansion reserves the inlinee's own frame, so a 16-byte array declared inside the inline helper should have reserved 16 per site. It reserved NOTHING - MWCC eliminated the unused array outright. The reservation had to be produced from the CALLER instead, as a pad declared last at function scope. Treat the inlinee-frame rule as describing what the ORIGINAL source did, not as a lever you can pull from inside the helper.
